name: Base: heat+flash benzene-toluene (valid)
description: Heat an equimolar benzene and toluene mixture from 25°C to 100°C at 1 atm, then flash-separate in a vessel.
notes: Unperturbed base case. Should converge on first attempt.

name: Mild over-heating: benzene-toluene heater +20K
description: Heat an equimolar benzene and toluene mixture from 25°C to 120°C at 1 atm, then flash. The outlet temperature is 20K above the nominal case — both components are near-fully vaporised.
notes: Mild perturbation. System should converge with minimal repair. Vapour fraction increases markedly.

name: Severe over-heating: benzene-toluene heater +80K
description: Heat an equimolar benzene and toluene mixture from 25°C to 180°C at 1 atm — well above the toluene boiling point (111°C). Flash the superheated vapour in a vessel. The system must detect that complete vaporisation occurs before the flash.
notes: Severe perturbation. At 180°C both components are fully vaporised — separator produces near-zero liquid. System must not flag this as a physics error.

name: Under-heating: benzene-toluene heater -20K
description: Heat an equimolar benzene and toluene mixture from 25°C to 80°C at 1 atm — just below benzene boiling point. The mixture is barely at the bubble point. Flash in a vessel.
notes: Mild under-heating. Near the bubble point, vapour fraction is low but nonzero. Should converge.

name: Invalid: heater outlet below inlet temperature
description: Process benzene and toluene through a heater and flash vessel, but specify the heater outlet temperature as 10°C — below the feed temperature of 25°C. The heater is acting as a cooler, which is physically contradictory.
notes: Tests detection and repair of an invalid parameter assignment. The system must recognise T_out < T_in for a heater as unphysical and correct it.

name: Base: heat+flash acetone-water (valid)
description: Heat an acetone and water feed (70 mol% acetone) from 20°C to 70°C at 1 atm, then flash-separate.
notes: Unperturbed base. Acetone bp=56°C, so heating to 70°C gives partial vaporisation.

name: Moderate over-heating: acetone-water heater +30K
description: Heat an acetone and water feed (70 mol% acetone) from 20°C to 100°C at 1 atm, then flash-separate. Temperature is 30K above base — acetone is fully vaporised, water partially.
notes: At 100°C acetone (bp=56°C) is entirely in vapour phase. Water partially vaporises depending on composition.

name: Pressure increase: acetone-water at 1.5 atm
description: Heat an acetone and water feed (70 mol% acetone) from 20°C to 70°C at 1.5 atm (50% above base pressure), then flash-separate. Higher pressure raises bubble point, reducing vapour fraction.
notes: Pressure perturbation shifts the bubble point. Should still produce two phases at 70°C and 1.5 atm.

name: Under-heating: acetone-water heater -25K
description: Heat an acetone and water feed (70 mol% acetone) from 20°C to only 45°C at 1 atm — below the acetone boiling point of 56°C. The flash produces little or no vapour.
notes: Below-bubble-point heating. At 45°C the mixture is subcooled, vapour fraction near zero. Should converge but flash is trivial.

name: Invalid: flash vessel operating below feed bubble point
description: Heat an acetone and water feed to 70°C then flash in a vessel set to 10°C — well below the flash inlet temperature. This temperature assignment on the separator is physically contradictory since the inlet stream is at 70°C.
notes: Separator temperature below inlet temperature is unphysical in an adiabatic flash. System must detect and correct.

name: Base: ethanol-water separation train (valid)
description: Process an ethanol-water feed (40 mol% ethanol) at 1 atm: heat from 25°C to 78°C, flash-separate in a vessel, cool the liquid bottoms to 30°C, then pump to 3 bar.
notes: Unperturbed medium-difficulty base.

name: Over-heating: ethanol-water heater +40K
description: Process an ethanol-water feed (40 mol% ethanol) at 1 atm: heat from 25°C to 118°C (40K above base), flash-separate, cool bottoms, pump. At 118°C essentially all ethanol and much of the water vaporise — flash split changes drastically.
notes: Strong perturbation for medium-coupling case. Heater over-shoot propagates: less liquid enters cooler, reducing cooler duty and changing pump inlet conditions.

name: Under-heating: ethanol-water heater -30K
description: Process an ethanol-water feed (40 mol% ethanol) at 1 atm: heat from 25°C to only 48°C (30K below base) — below the ethanol boiling point. Flash produces very little vapour. Cool bottoms to 30°C and pump.
notes: Under-heating means negligible flash. Cooler has minimal duty. Tests whether pipeline handles near-zero vapour fractions gracefully.

name: Pressure doubling: ethanol-water at 2 atm
description: Process an ethanol-water feed (40 mol% ethanol) at 2 atm (double base pressure): heat from 25°C to 78°C, flash-separate (bubble point is higher at 2 atm, so less vapour forms), cool bottoms to 30°C, pump to 4 bar.
notes: At 2 atm the ethanol-water bubble point rises above 78°C — very little vapour forms. Tests pressure perturbation propagation through the whole 4-unit train.

name: Invalid: pump before cooler (wrong order)
description: Process an ethanol-water feed (40 mol% ethanol): heat to 78°C, flash-separate, then pump the liquid bottoms to 3 bar BEFORE cooling them. The pump is operating on a hot two-phase stream, which is unphysical for a liquid pump.
notes: Topology error: hot two-phase stream entering a liquid pump causes cavitation. System must detect invalid phase at pump inlet and either correct topology or add a cooler before the pump.

name: Base: near-azeotrope ethanol-water (valid)
description: Process an ethanol-water feed at 92 mol% ethanol — near the atmospheric azeotrope — by heating from 25°C to 78°C and flashing in a separator at 1 atm.
notes: High-difficulty base. Requires accurate NRTL BIPs for near-azeotropic behaviour.

name: Mild over-heating: near-azeotrope ethanol-water +10K
description: Process an ethanol-water feed at 92 mol% ethanol by heating to 88°C (+10K above nominal) and flashing. Near the azeotrope, even a 10K error in heater temperature can invert the vapour-liquid split.
notes: Critical case: near-azeotrope VLE is highly sensitive to temperature. +10K may push composition to wrong side of azeotrope curve. Tests whether BIPs and repair prevent composition inversion.

name: Mild under-heating: near-azeotrope ethanol-water -10K
description: Process an ethanol-water feed at 92 mol% ethanol by heating to only 68°C (-10K below nominal). At this temperature, the mixture may not reach its bubble point — near-zero vapour fraction expected.
notes: At 68°C the 92 mol% ethanol mixture may be subcooled (bubble point ~78°C). Tests flash with near-zero vapour or all-liquid result.

name: Invalid package: near-azeotrope with Raoult's Law
description: Process an ethanol-water feed at 92 mol% ethanol — near-azeotrope — using Raoult's Law as the property package. This is physically incorrect (the mixture has strong non-ideal interactions) and will produce wrong VLE predictions.
notes: Critical: using Raoult's Law for ethanol-water completely misses the azeotrope. The system must detect the wrong package and switch to NRTL with BIPs. Tests the thermo-package repair path.

name: Severe over-heating: near-azeotrope ethanol-water +80K
description: Process an ethanol-water feed at 92 mol% ethanol by heating to 158°C — 80K above the azeotrope boiling point. At this temperature the mixture is entirely superheated vapour. Flash separation produces no liquid.
notes: Severe perturbation. Entire mixture is vapour at 158°C and 1 atm. Flash vessel produces no liquid product. Tests handling of all-vapour flash.
